subject: Intermittent p99 spikes & elevated 5xxs during peak — ClearPay impact
messages:
From: Claire Hodgson <claire.hodgson@clearpay.com>
To: ethan_park@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@clearpay.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Aug 2029 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production slowdowns the last 48h — urgent

Hi Ethan,

We started seeing intermittent slowdowns yesterday afternoon and they got worse overnight. Users are getting long checkouts and we see p99 latency jump from ~850ms to 6–8s in short bursts, plus an uptick in 5xx errors. This is affecting conversion on our checkout flow.

I attached a small sample of request logs and a screenshot of our analytics chart. Can your team confirm whether this is on Redwood's side (queueing/capacity) or something on our integration? We need a clear action plan and ETA — this is starting to hit the weekly ops review.

Thanks,
Claire Hodgson
VP, Engineering — ClearPay

Attachments: clearpay_request_logs.csv, p99_dashboard_capture.png

From: ethan_park@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Aug 2029 17:05:24 -0700
Subject: Re: Production slowdowns the last 48h — urgent

Hi Claire — thanks for the heads up and the logs; we see the same spikes on our side in the ClearPay tenant. I've looped in Marissa (AM) and Vivek (SRE). First pass: this looks like long-tail queueing coincident with your batch reconciliation jobs that start at :45 past the hour — we see concentration of large multi-input requests that grow the batch window and push some requests into the slow path.

Immediate next steps:
- Vivek to validate whether concurrency caps or backpressure are tripping and causing slow completions.
- We'll provision a short-term burst pool (10% headroom) and shadow route a subset of traffic to observe effect.
- Share an exec-facing summary and schedule a 30-min call if we need to escalate to leadership.

I'll follow up with data within 90 minutes.

—Ethan
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: ethan_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Aug 2029 17:37:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Production slowdowns the last 48h — urgent

Quick triage notes:
- I confirmed elevated queuing depth around 16:20–18:10 PDT and again after 01:45 UTC. The distribution shows a heavy right tail — a small fraction of requests (0.8%) are occupying resources for much longer than median.
- Concurrency caps for ClearPay pool were hit intermittently at 88% of configured limit; we saw automatic backpressure start to apply which moves requests into a slow retry/queue path.
- Root cause candidate: large multi-part messages from ClearPay's reconciliation job cause higher token counts and longer KV-cache handling, which interacts poorly with current batching thresholds.

Actions taken (done now):
1) Temporarily increased concurrency cap for ClearPay pool by +12% (10 min warm-up).
2) Enabled prefix KV caching optimization for the model variant serving them.
3) Spun up a small burst pool and shadowed 5% of traffic; initial 20-minute window shows p99 dropping from ~6.2s to ~1.1s for shadowed requests.

Still to do:
- Collect end-to-end traces for the 5xxs to rule out application-level errors at their side (I suspect some downstream timeouts).
- Recommend a follow-up config change: reduce max batch window from 120ms to 60ms for this pool and treat long-sequence requests with a separate route.

I'll assemble graphs and forward to Claire. If we keep seeing reappearing spikes after 24h, we should book an exec sync.

—Vivek
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 8 Aug 2029 09:12:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Production slowdowns the last 48h — urgent

Claire —
Thanks for raising this. Appreciate the logs. Implementation notes / ask from ClearPay: could you confirm whether the reconciliation jobs started a new code path on Aug 6 (new batching logic)? Also, can your team try reducing the concurrency of those jobs for a 2-hour window to see if that mitigates the tail?

We're going to hold the temporary burst capacity for 12 hours while we monitor, and we're preparing an ops playbook entry that lists:
- How we detect long-tail growth
- Short-term mitigation (burst pool + concurrency bump)
- Medium-term route (split heavy sequences to a heavier quantized variant)

If p99 remains high after the adjustments Vivek proposed, I will request an exec triage at 11:00 PT today and loop our infra leadership. Hoping it doesn't get that far.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Manager — Redwood Inference

Claire — quick update after 36h monitoring:
- The temporary burst pool and concurrency bump cut the observed p99 for shadowed traffic to ~900–1.2s consistently; production p99 improved but we still see re-emergent spikes at times tied to your large reconciliation runs.
- 5xx rate dropped by ~70% after we adjusted the batching window and enabled the KV caching optimization. Remaining 5xxs correlate with a specific request pattern; your logs show a small set of requests timing out at your downstream callback URL.

Next steps and ask:
- Can ClearPay throttle the reconciliation job concurrency by 40% for the next two cycles to validate the hypothesis? If you can, we will simultaneously route that workload to a quantized model variant that handles larger sequences without impacting median latency.
- If throttling is not possible, we recommend an executive sync today at 11:00 PT so we can authorize 2 hours of elevated burst capacity and tie it to a coordinated mitigation schedule.

I've attached the escalation runbook and the datadog capture. If you confirm the throttling test, we'll run it and report results within 90 minutes.

—Ethan Park

Redwood Inference
